scope: Entire supplied Chapter 1 reading preview compared with immutable source and accepted Option B directions; all thirty audit dispositions. No Chapter 2, rendered artwork or unapproved production asset reviewed.
assessment: No remaining blocking textual contradiction was identified in this Chapter 1 proposal against the accepted Option B directions. This is a limited editorial assessment, not manuscript approval or a guarantee of creative quality. Continuation and production dependencies remain open.

checks.assessment: The narration does not name Tomas before he introduces himself. Both introductions still precede the scratched-name exchange. Lilia and Arturo remain the supplied prose names; no aliases, murder proof, death proof or invented biography are inserted.

The customer counter and back-wall hatch stay distinct. Tomas moves into his own kitchen; Daniel walks around his own ruined counter. His floor and door remain ruined/painted. Closure removes the past view rather than destroying newly restored present furnishings. Exact visual geometry remains unapproved.

Shared tray returns to Tomas; jointly held saucer ages only after release and complete forward transfer; the backward sleeve stays crisp. The unstable-counter painful touch and stable-hatch warm touch remain distinct. The first note stays in Tomas's apron, while the notebook page returns. No preservation spell, repeated-aging exploit or bodily crossing is declared.

All eight standalone markers 12:00 through 12:07 remain in order. Tomas visibly writes and releases the reply before closure. Its corner catches on Daniel's side and falls free afterward. The handwritten reply is read after the room goes dark, so the emotional reveal survives. Event feasibility has been read editorially, not validated by timed actors.

Flashlight placement, carrying, fall and recovery are explicit. The folder follows Daniel to the hatch; the saucer is set down before writing; the token stays by the original counter. Daniel keeps his broken pencil, while a disclosed minor new apron pencil gives Tomas a writing tool. No missing prop recovery or image reference is invented.

Late access has a permit/clearance reason; it does not schedule demolition or the historical fire. The year is a file-based guess before Tomas answers. Both signal and broker are recorded; redevelopment explains attention, not guilt. Daniel already knows the service corridor from the archive, and the ending does not claim otherwise.

The unchanged archive prelude turns routine inventory into suspected concealment. The station scene changes knowledge, fear, trust and the intention to meet again. Occupational banter, chosen-family joke, distinct note exchanges, Tomas's reciprocal reply, broken laugh and final warning remain. One repeated hair paragraph is trimmed; extra handling makes the chapter longer, so reader pacing remains untested.

The package is a revisions-only proposal with a readable text preview. Source, previous packages and active versions remain unchanged. Only the actual Option B plan/policy approval is recorded. No exact-change approval, canon adoption, stage lock, artwork, image job or online publication is inferred.

warnings.message: The preview adds 241 whitespace-delimited story words, from 2655 to 2896 (about 9.1%). Most additions are continuity handling. No timed read or reader feedback has tested their effect; the 12:02 movement/test beat and 12:06 writing beat deserve particular attention.

Resolve Daniel's calendar date, recurrence mapping, fire deadline, meeting count and precise historical-warning costs before a new chapter depends on them. First contact still lasts seven minutes; no 17-second deduction or recovery rule is selected.
Scratch authorship and the first photograph's contents remain unknown. A later photo comparison is still owed; this repair cannot supply or infer its result.

The late-access addition creates a practical next-visit problem: Daniel's permit expires and loose fittings face clearance. It does not mean the entire station is demolished that morning. A continuation must address access and preservation instead of silently renewing the permit or ignoring clearance.
Legacy page prompts still contain the old identity, missing-dialogue and layout problems. They are immutable sources, not repaired production assets. No approved images or Chapter 2 are present.
There is no adopted canon or active approved manuscript. Accepted directions constrain the proposal, but formal canon adoption and all stage locks remain separate user decisions.
Audience, historical setting detail, content rating, reader response and commercial assumptions have not been externally tested. No manuscript search, upload or research was performed.

issue_dispositions.reason: Chapter 2 and claimed images are absent. Approved scope is only the available Chapter 1; no new material is invented.
issue_dispositions.diagnostic_description: README, arc notes, and series plan claim a drafted Chapter 2 and Chapter 1 reader images. The root inventory contains only Chapter 1 prose, fourteen interior page prompts, three cover prompts including the app cover, and supporting notes; no reader image files or second chapter are present.

issue_dispositions.reason: Lilia is accepted for derivatives and retained in prose. The old Inez page prompt is untouched and must be reconciled in new manga scripts.
issue_dispositions.diagnostic_description: The prose calls the kitchen voice Tiya Lilia, and the character reference identifies Lilia Ramos as the cafe owner and chosen aunt. Page 10 assigns the same lines and role to Inez without explanation.

issue_dispositions.reason: Arturo is accepted for derivatives and retained in prose. Rafael in the legacy prompt is not treated as an alias.
issue_dispositions.diagnostic_description: The prose and character reference name Arturo Salcedo as the visiting broker. Page 11 instead labels the figure and notebook entry Rafael Aragon while retaining Arturo's physical and behavioral traits.

issue_dispositions.reason: The prose introductions already precede the name clue and remain unchanged. New manga scripts must restore the omitted exchange.
issue_dispositions.diagnostic_description: The prose introduces Daniel and Tomas by name before Daniel recognizes TOMAS on the door. Pages 5-7 omit that exchange, but Page 7 has Daniel say I FOUND YOUR NAME. Character-lock text is not reader-facing dialogue.

issue_dispositions.reason: Hatch location, own-era movement and post-move surface names are explicit. Source and legacy scripts remain unchanged.
issue_dispositions.diagnostic_description: The service window is behind the counter and opens into the kitchen, yet later opens between the two men, who are already on opposite sides of a shared counter. No movement explains how both access opposite faces of that window.

issue_dispositions.reason: The past environment appears beyond shared surfaces; Daniel's room remains ruined at opening and closure.
issue_dispositions.diagnostic_description: The prose first says the painted glass clears and broken stools stand upright, then says Daniel's side remains ruined and the painted door still carries the scratch. Page 4 similarly restores objects around Daniel before later split-era staging.

issue_dispositions.reason: Tomas writes and returns the paper before 12:07; its caught corner falls free only after it is already on Daniel's side.
issue_dispositions.diagnostic_description: After 12:07, closure, and several seconds alone, Daniel's notebook page slips from the sealed window with Tomas's reply. The stated exchange rules restrict the reliable connection to seven minutes.

issue_dispositions.reason: Shared possession, completed forward aging and unchanged backward transfer are concrete. Repeated transfer and other untested rule edges remain undecided.
issue_dispositions.diagnostic_description: The rules permit objects to avoid forty years of aging if protected by the interval, but the pastry ages while the interval is active. Backward objects later adapt to the older time, without a defined trigger or physical effect. The preserved note and ordinary notebook page are separate objects.

issue_dispositions.reason: First meeting is still the full seven minutes. Accepted cost direction requires exact calibration before future historical intervention.
issue_dispositions.diagnostic_description: Direct warnings shorten the connection; coded clues do less damage but the cafe understands intent. Minute loss does not recover easily, implying unspecified recovery. No supplied scene establishes a baseline cost, threshold, or distinction between ordinary flicker and permanent loss.

issue_dispositions.reason: No unsupported calendar or fire date is added. The private calendar remains required before Chapter 2.
issue_dispositions.diagnostic_description: Tomas gives October 17, 1986, and Daniel gives only 2026. The opening says 11:41 PM but does not establish Daniel's calendar date. Notes describe both nightly recurrence and two specific nights; the fire's exact date and how successive meetings advance each era are unavailable.

issue_dispositions.reason: Daniel's 1986 inference is explicitly anchored to the fire report and remains a guess until Tomas states the date.
issue_dispositions.diagnostic_description: Before Tomas states the year, the close Daniel narration says the kitchen lived in 1986 and that he knew it before proof. His archives are from 1986, but the visible cafe details do not uniquely establish that year.

issue_dispositions.reason: Daniel records the failed signal and the broker; redevelopment motivates attention without implying guilt.
issue_dispositions.diagnostic_description: Daniel singles out the white suit from a list that also includes a failed signal. The opening evidence contains no stated white-suit connection, and Page 11 labels the broker as a suspect or important clue.

issue_dispositions.reason: The prose already presents a personal warning, not newly learned corridor location or murder proof. The false legacy adaptation emphasis must be repaired later.
issue_dispositions.diagnostic_description: Page 14 says Daniel found a warning the official archive did not contain and depicts the moment as a murder mystery. The opening archive already places the fire in the service corridor. The new fact is the scratched warning's form, apparent age, and proximity to TOMAS, not a new corridor location or confirmed murder.

issue_dispositions.reason: A final evening permit and morning loose-fitting clearance explain why Daniel records the site late. Next-visit access becomes a continuation obligation.
issue_dispositions.diagnostic_description: Daniel has permits and an archive assignment, but his choice to inspect the damaged station alone at 11:41 PM has no concrete deadline, access constraint, or immediate objective beyond inventory.

issue_dispositions.reason: Tomas retains initiative and the new visible reply action. His accepted cafe/chosen-family goal needs later architecture, not invented exposition in this opening.
issue_dispositions.diagnostic_description: Tomas acts in Chapter 1: he offers bread, asks for a return object, and agrees to meet again. The reference emphasizes his warmth, concealed loneliness, and status as a target, but gives no concrete personal goal that can conflict with Daniel's rescue plan.

issue_dispositions.reason: Daniel's emotional restraint and professional defenses remain. No dead lover or other invented trauma is supplied as an explanation.
issue_dispositions.diagnostic_description: Daniel trusts paper more than people, presents I am real, and fears losing the encounter. Notes prescribe adults carrying grief but supply no event explaining his isolation or a particular bereavement.

issue_dispositions.reason: Witness knowledge, costs and choices need versioned future architecture. The opening does not invent absent witnesses' secrets.
issue_dispositions.diagnostic_description: Maribel will notice changing records, Lilia may hide an object, Benjamin leaves conflicting testimony, Ernesto misremembers, and Arturo may have arranged arson. The notes do not yet connect their specific knowledge, choices, incentives, and costs.

issue_dispositions.reason: Preserved discoveries are recorded as already known; future plotting must not repeat them as first discoveries.
issue_dispositions.diagnostic_description: Chapter 1 already ages a pastry and shows falsified-looking records. Chapter 5 is titled The Pastry That Aged Forty Years; Arc 2 again promises evidence of falsified fire records. Arc 1 includes The Man Who Bought The Station Fire and a burning-twice climax, while Arc 3 revisits the man behind the fire and Arc 6 the repeating year.

issue_dispositions.reason: Opening three-unit checkpoint and provisional fifteen-title arc remain planning boundaries; 105 chapters are not a fixed production commitment.
issue_dispositions.diagnostic_description: The series plan recommends seven equal fifteen-chapter arcs and possible expansion to 150 chapters. The available story is one drafted chapter; no scene-level long-series architecture, production capacity, reader feedback, or release calendar is supplied.

issue_dispositions.reason: Other cafes are not introduced; any expansion must protect the central relationship and justify a distinct purpose.
issue_dispositions.diagnostic_description: The premise calls the cafe a fragile connection between two specific nights. Arc 4 proposes other seven-minute crossings at abandoned railway sites without a rationale that connects them to Daniel and Tomas's choices.

issue_dispositions.reason: No reset occurs. Later reset proposals must preserve earned intimacy and consequences.
issue_dispositions.diagnostic_description: Arc 5 has Tomas no longer remember Daniel clearly, Arc 6 repeats fragments of 1986, and the final arc again asks which future can survive. Without persistent changes, these devices may repeatedly undo earned intimacy.

issue_dispositions.diagnostic_description: Existing prompts request whole pages with gutters, dialogue, captions, and SFX inside generated images. The current request requires structured versioned jobs, panel artwork without lettering or borders, and separate approved downstream composition.

issue_dispositions.reason: Geometry-only nemu, event-driven panels and reading order depend on approved story text. No fixed 75-panel layout is adopted.

Page 8 packs painful touch, a moving window, a joke, a pastry crossing, aging, and both reactions into six panels. No explicit reading direction, panel geometry, or dialogue-safe zones is supplied.

issue_dispositions.reason: The prose question/answer chains and signal clue remain, with both investigative leads now explicit. New manga scripts must preserve them.
issue_dispositions.diagnostic_description: Page 6 jumps from Museum conservator to Possessed and then the year without the prose's year question and defensive exchange. Page 7 begins Your side without its original prompting line. Page 11 omits the failed southbound signal while isolating the broker.

issue_dispositions.reason: Flashlight and folder custody are repaired; cafe/railway clocks stay separate and source rolled sleeves remain. Legacy visual conflicts require new scripts/references later.
issue_dispositions.diagnostic_description: The cafe clock is above the door in prose and Page 4 but above the menu board in characters.md; a separate station clock exists. The prose drops the flashlight at 12:04, but Page 10 omits that beat and Page 13 places it on the floor. Tomas's reference specifies a short-sleeved shirt while prose repeatedly describes sleeves rolled to the elbows.

issue_dispositions.reason: Prose sound sources remain readable, but full structured SFX and lettering intent belong to approved manga scripting.
issue_dispositions.diagnostic_description: The scripts include DRIP, KREEEAK, CLICK, FWOOM, CLINK, TICK, ZZT, CLACK, KRRK, WHUMP, FSSHT, and SSHHH, but do not consistently specify source, reader meaning, intensity, language, translation context, and lettering intent. Page 7 places TICK with a coffee-ring image rather than an explicit clock shot.

issue_dispositions.reason: One repeated hair movement is removed; dry humor, material detail and other signature descriptions are preserved. No global stylistic flattening is attempted.
issue_dispositions.diagnostic_description: The chapter repeatedly notes Tomas's fallen hair and pairs many emotional or sensory beats with figurative interpretation. This establishes a recognizable voice, but some repetition can slow a seven-minute scene or become redundant when drawn.

issue_dispositions.reason: English LTR paged format and adult romantic-thriller audience direction are accepted. Country stays unnamed and market/historical assumptions remain untested.
issue_dispositions.diagnostic_description: The text uses Filipino-coded names, Tiya, pan de leche, municipal redevelopment, and 1986, while only Maribel is explicitly described as Filipina-Spanish. No country, city model, period-research dossier, formal rating, platform, or romance ending commitment is supplied.

issue_dispositions.reason: Scratch author and photo contents stay unknown. Later comparison is required for a fair claim of a changed warning.
issue_dispositions.diagnostic_description: Daniel photographs the TOMAS scratch before the encounter. Later dust reveals FIRE STARTS IN THE SERVICE CORRIDOR beneath it. The current text does not establish whether the second line was physically obscured, newly changed, or present in the first photograph, and its author is unknown.
